summary: Multiplexed websocket fanout produces trailing partial-fragment and client silent-reconnect loop behind corporate edge appliance
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports repeated short-lived websocket sessions from browser clients after high-volume multiplexed fanout (server-side sends same delta to ~40 clients). Affected sessions show a trailing 1-3 byte partial JSON fragment followed by an immediate silent reconnect loop (client reconnects but receives duplicate prefix tokens). Impact: several of customer's chat widgets display incomplete final sentences or duplicate prefixes, causing UX corruption and elevated error rates in their monitoring.

Impact:
- Partial outputs (incomplete last sentence) for ~12% of streaming requests during peak traffic windows (spikes to 1.2k RPS).
- Clients disconnect and reconnect automatically, resulting in doubled token consumption for a subset of flows and billing concerns.

Environment and constraints:
- Customer on enterprise Dedicated plan using private VPC egress through their edge appliance (A10/F5 managed by customer).
- Connections use websocket upgrades via our API gateway with HTTP/2 termination at the edge appliance and h1 to our gateway in the backend.

Observed behavior:
- Server sends well-formed JSON choice end event but client receives a final partial chunk (1-3 bytes) that cannot be parsed by the SDK JSON stream assembler.
- Client SDK shows an immediate reconnect with identical session-id; on reconnection the first chunks re-play the duplicated prefix tokens then stream continues (duplicate content + missing final clause).

Expected behavior:
- Client should receive full terminal chunk and not auto-reconnect due to malformed framing. No duplicate prefix replay on subsequent reconnects.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer configured multiplexed fanout: single model response broadcast to ~40 web clients using websocket multiplexing IDs.
2) Send long-running generation with trailing punctuation and multi-sentence finale (~400 tokens).
3) Observe on some clients: final JSON choice event arrives truncated by a few bytes, SDK JSON parser fails to finalize and triggers reconnect logic.
4) Reconnect receives prefix replays and duplicated token sequences before normal continuation.
logs: edge-proxy (customer) tcpdump: observed HTTP/2 HEADERS + multiple DATA frames coalesced and then forwarded as single HTTP/1.1 chunk sequence to our gateway
gateway access log: ws upgrade successful -> stream id 0x7f3a; final write to socket shows 3 bytes less than server-side payload size
serving-runtime trace: choice-end event emitted at 2026-03-10T16:02:34.752Z size=312 bytes; low-level socket write returned size=309 bytes (on connection path with appliance).
client SDK logs (customer): JSONStreamAssembler error: Unfinished token at EOF. Triggering reconnect. SDK v1.14.2.
metrics: customer saw 2.1x reconnect rate for streaming connections between 16:00-16:20 PDT on 2026-03-10.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: gzip/Brotli or proxy buffer coalescing at the appliance is trimming or splitting chunk boundaries leading to incomplete final frames.

Reproduced in-house by inserting an HTTP/2 -> HTTP/1.1 conversion proxy (nginx with http2 upstream) and high-fanout payloads; saw final DATA frame coalesced with keepalive and truncated by 1-4 bytes under certain buffering flags.

Correlation observed: issue only when customer's appliance performs HTTP/2 termination and uses 'http2-max-concurrent-streams' lower than our gateway defaults; reassembly window misaligned leading to drop of tail bytes on edge rewrite.
SDK behavior: on partial final JSON the assembler marks stream as corrupt and triggers immediate reconnect (no exponential backoff configured in customer's integration).
Not reproduced when bypassing appliance (direct path) or when using SSE long-poll fallback.
comments: 2026-03-10 19:05 - Support (Aisha): Asked customer for tcpdump from their egress appliance and full client SDK logs. Provided temporary instrumentation snippet for more detailed ws frame logging.
2026-03-10 20:30 - Customer (L. Chen, Northbridge): Uploaded tcpdump and confirmed appliance vendor support will review h2->h1 translation settings.
2026-03-11 09:12 - SRE (Tomás): Reproduced locally with nginx proxy config; created minimal repro harness (link to test harness in repo PR).

2026-03-11 11:40 - SRE (Tomás): Deployed temporary mitigation in gateway: added toleration for trailing partial fragment by buffering up-to 12 bytes and attempting JSON resync. Reduced observed client disconnects in controlled test from 18% to 2%.

2026-03-12 08:47 - Customer (L. Chen): Appliance vendor identified configuration option 'proxy_buffering on' + HTTP/2 coalescing as likely root cause and will apply a patch to preserve DATA frame boundaries.

2026-03-12 15:20 - Support (Aisha): Recommended customer apply appliance vendor patch and also update their client SDK to implement a short exponential backoff (500ms -> 1s) to avoid back-to-back reconnect storms.
2026-03-13 10:05 - SRE (Tomás): Noted follow-up: adjust gateway buffering change into a feature flag for controlled rollout. Created INT-4122 to track gateway code change and tests.
resolution: Workaround applied: gateway buffering tolerance enabled for affected connections (feature-flagged); attempted to silently reassemble small trailing fragments up to 12 bytes and deliver final event when valid JSON can be reconstructed.
Customer action: applied vendor patch to edge appliance to preserve HTTP/2 DATA frame boundaries and disabled aggressive coalescing. Vendor confirmed patch will be rolled to prod on 2026-03-14.

Client recommendation: upgrade SDK to v1.15.0 which includes safer reconnect backoff and a parser fallback that attempts a one-shot small-buffer reassemble before reconnecting (decreases duplicate-prefix replay).

Root cause: appliance HTTP/2->HTTP/1 translation + buffer coalescing/truncation produced 1-4 byte tail loss on final DATA frames for high-fanout websocket payloads. SDK immediate reconnect logic amplified the impact by replaying prefixes and doubling token usage.

Follow-ups: INT-4122 (gateway buffering feature) for bounded reassembly; QA tests added to streaming regression suite to simulate h2->h1 conversion appliances; postmortem checklist entry to include advising enterprise customers on appliance configs for websocket paths.
